answer: PostgreSQL manages transactions on the remote server using `SERIALIZABLE` isolation level when the local transaction is also `SERIALIZABLE`, otherwise it uses `REPEATABLE READ`. This ensures snapshot-consistent results for queries that perform multiple table scans on the remote server, meaning successive queries within a single transaction will see the same data even if updates occur concurrently on the remote server. This behavior can be surprising for `READ COMMITTED` local transactions [citations: 1, 2].
